metadata.note: The Lake Superior and Ishpeming family in Michigan's Upper Peninsula: the Munising Railway (Munising - Lawson - Little Lake, later Princeton, and the East Branch), the Marquette and Southeastern (Lawson - Marquette and the Big Bay branch), their April 1911 consolidation the Munising, Marquette and Southeastern, the Lake Superior and Ishpeming itself (Marquette - Negaunee - Ishpeming from 1898, and the whole system after absorbing the MM&SE in 1923), and the Marquette and Huron Mountain steam tourist line on the ex-LS&I Big Bay branch (1964, 1966). Features are split by operator era (Rule 4) and by drawable span; split features share identical geometry and the boundary year is drawn on both sides. Every span drawn is the research report's drawable span, NOT the wider pax_start/pax_end bracket. Cleveland-Cliffs' stock control (1899/1900 of the Munising Railway; the LS&I throughout) is not a split. The LS&I's ore lines (Humboldt, Republic, Tilden, Maas, Gwinn-district mine branches), logging spurs, and every line's post-passenger freight years are freight only and are not drawn (Rule 1). Research report: research/branches/lake_superior_and_ishpeming_railroad.txt.

not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] ends: Munising - Lawson and Lawson - Marquette end at 1951 (last confirmed, Feb 1951 Guide); Lawson - Little Lake and Little Lake - Princeton end at 1937 (Fowler 1937 company timetable); Marquette - Ishpeming and Ishpeming - North Lake end at 1929 (Oct 1929 Guide). The actual end of LS&I passenger service (Wikipedia, uncited: Munising - Princeton only by 1955, none by 1960; an unverified '3 July 1957') is unsourced. Best next sources: Durocher, R&LHS Bulletin 98 (1958); Dorin, The Lake Superior Iron Ore Railroads (1969); Marquette Mining Journal / Escanaba Daily Press 1955-1960 for an MPSC discontinuance.

[OPEN] starts: Munising - Lawson and Lawson - Little Lake from 1901 (opened 1896/1897); Lawson - Marquette from 1902 (M&SE opening date not found); Big Bay branch from 1909 (built 1905-06); Princeton extension from 1929 (built 1906 - no Munising Railway or MM&SE feature drawn there); North Lake from 1914.

[ANCHOR] single proven years: East Branch Stillman - Cusino 1929 only (start and end unknown; Feb 1951 heading without times); M&HM Marquette - Big Bay 1964 only (1965 season conflicted: Sept 1965 photo vs 'stopped the previous year'); M&HM Marquette - Harlow Lake 1966 only (daily schedule announced vs 'only one excursion').
CONFLICT: MM&SE absorbed by the LS&I in 1923 (Meints p.115 via Wikipedia; michiganrailroads MM&SE page; Mid-Continent) vs 1924 (michiganrailroads LS&I timeline; american-rails). Split drawn at 1923.
CONFLICT: Munising Railway opened 30 Nov 1897 (michiganrailroads) vs December 1896 (american-rails). Moot for the map, which starts at 1901.
1911-1923 (MM&SE era) has no timetable read for any line; those segments rest on continuity between 1909 and 1929.
Marquette - Ishpeming end bracket 1929-1945 (1945 MPSC: no regularly scheduled passenger trains); Mid-Continent's 'passenger service ended on the LS&I in 1929' may apply to this line only.
Was Marquette - Lawson dropped in the Aug 1953 MPSC Big Bay case or separately?
Big Bay branch frequency cut to three a week dated 'by 1940' only by uncited Wikipedia.
Location of the LS&I Marquette passenger depot not established; drawn at a hand-pinned downtown point. North Lake station site not established.
headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates throughout (see each segment note and speed_source).

segments.note: Munising Railway main line Munising - Merriam - Munising Junction - Stillman - Vail - Dixon - Slapneck - Chatham - Eben - Rumely - Dorsey - Lawson. Opened Munising - Little Lake 30 Nov 1897 [MRR-MUN] (american-rails: 'finished in December 1896' - CONFLICT, moot here). [OPEN] START: 1901 is the first CONFIRMED passenger year (MRC-1901: 33,294 passenger-train miles and 27,484 mixed-train miles on the Munising Railway [MRR-MUN]); service may have begun earlier (the line opened 1896/1897), but no earlier year is proven. Do not extend without evidence. 1902: through Ishpeming - Marquette - Munising passenger service begun jointly with the M&SE and LS&I [MRR-MSE quoting MCR-1903]; 1903: 6 stations, 5 passenger cars [MCR-1905 via MRR-MUN]; 1909: track 'in fair condition' [MRR-1909]. Cleveland-Cliffs bought control 1899/1900 - a stock purchase; the trains stayed Munising Railway trains, so it is not a split. Split at 1911: the Munising Railway and the Marquette and Southeastern were consolidated as the Munising, Marquette and Southeastern in April 1911 (WP-MMSE, citing Meints 1992 p.115). The boundary year 1911 is drawn on both features, as the repo's other split files do. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (no timetable of 1901-1911 was read).
sources: Segment-level: start 1901 = first confirmed passenger year (MRC-1901 train-miles via MRR-MUN); end 1911 = April 1911 consolidation (WP-MMSE, citing Meints). 1902/1903/1909 evidence from MRR-MSE, MRR-MUN, MRR-1909. Headway not sourced (estimate).

segments.note: Late LS&I service, mixed trains. 1946 employee timetable: daily-except-Sunday mixed, Marquette 5:05 a.m., Lawson 6:50, Munising 9:00; return Munising 3:30 p.m., Lawson 5:35 [MRR-TT-ML, AR]. Feb 1951 Official Guide: the LS&I main table ('February, 1951'), Munising - Merriam - Munising Junc - Stillman - Rumely - Dorsey - Harvey - Marquette, prints times ([GUIDE]; no motor-coach or freight-only wording on the page). Do not extend without evidence. Freight continued (abandonment sought 1976; east of Marquette abandoned 1979 except Munising Jct - Munising, Wisconsin Central 1990) - context, not drawn. headway_min = one train a day (1946 ETT).
sources: Segment-level: 1946 mixed train from the 1946 ETT (MRR-TT-ML, AR); end 1951 = last confirmed year, the Feb 1951 timed table in the Feb 1952 Official Guide [GUIDE]. The start year 1938 is only the frequency break, not a sourced date.

PRE-1965 ALIGNMENT: the trace goes north via Forestville on the original LS&I corridor and does not follow the 1965 US-41 consolidation; about 10 mi of it coincides with track still in use today (Presque Isle - Forestville and parts toward Eagle Mills), which is the same corridor, not a relocation, as far as OHM shows. Not verified against a pre-1965 map at Negaunee, where the LS&I made a late-1890s relocation; the drawn Negaunee alignment is OHM's. It is a SEPARATE track from the DSS&A/MH&O Marquette - Negaunee - Ishpeming line (feature mho-marquette-negaunee-ishpeming): only 0.2 mi lies within 40 m of that feature, at Negaunee. Between Negaunee and Ishpeming 1.4 mi lies within 40 m of the C&NW Peninsula Division feature, which runs in the same narrow corridor; the trace is on LS&I/untagged OHM ways there, not C&NW-named ones. Waypoints: Forestville 0.0 km, Eagle Mills 0.3, Negaunee 0.1, Ishpeming 0.2. segments.note: The original LS&I, opened Presque Isle - Negaunee - Ishpeming in Aug 1896 as an ore road; it ran no passenger trains until right-of-way grantors went to court [LAS-1898-0604], so 1896-1897 are NOT drawn (freight only). 1898 exact: 'The first passenger train over the Lake Superior and Ishpeming Railroad went over the line, carrying prominent citizens of Ishpeming and Negaunee' (BHN-1898-0611 via MRR-LSI); two Pullman coaches bought 1898 for excursion service Ishpeming - Presque Isle [AR]; service suspended Dec 1898 'until spring' (IWT-1898-1210) - a winter gap inside the drawn span. 1902: through Ishpeming - Munising service with the M&SE and Munising Railway; 1903: 4 passenger cars [MCR-1903]; 1904: over 180,000 passenger-miles [WP-LSI]. 'Really commuter trains serving Ishpeming, Negaunee and Marquette' [MRR-ISH]; Marquette passengers reached Presque Isle by streetcar [AR]. 1905-1913 and 1915-1928 rest on continuity between dated anchors (1898, 1902-04, 1909, 1914, 1929). Oct 1929: train 11 Lawson 8:35 AM - Marquette 9:50 - West Yard - Forestville - Eagle Mills - Negaunee - Ishpeming 12:30 PM - North Lake, train 12 back from Ishpeming 1:00 PM, daily except Sunday [OG30]. [OPEN] END: 1929 is the last CONFIRMED passenger year (the Oct 1929 schedules in the Jan 1930 Official Guide), NOT a known end - no source dates when service actually stopped (by 1945 the LS&I told the MPSC it had no regularly scheduled passenger trains Marquette - Ishpeming [MRR-LSI]; Mid-Continent's 'passenger service ended on the LS&I in 1929' is wrong system-wide and unsourced for this line; Fowler gives Negaunee/Ishpeming no 1937 tag, which is absence, not evidence). Do not extend without evidence. The LS&I was one company throughout (Railway to 1923, Railroad after) - no split. This duplicated the DSS&A and C&NW Marquette - Ishpeming service on a separate, parallel track. headway_min = the one 1929 train each way; earlier commuter service was probably more frequent but no count was found.
sources: Segment-level: start 1898 = first passenger train (BHN-1898-0611 and LAS-1898-0604 via MRR-LSI; AR); end 1929 = last confirmed year, Oct 1929 schedules in the Jan 1930 Guide [OG30]; 1902-1904 from MCR-1903/WP-LSI. The years between anchors rest on continuity.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 22.7 mi against about 23.6 mi documented (Fowler 8.4 - 32; [OG30] Stillman mile 9, Cusino mile 32). Router breakdown: 22.4 mi LS&I-family (OHM 1897-1969), 0.2 mi OHM:(untagged). 'LS&I-family (OHM ...)' = OpenHistoricalMap ways named for the LS&I or Munising Railway, with their OHM date tags; 'LS&I (OSM grade/trail)' = OSM abandoned grades tagged or named Lake Superior and Ishpeming; '(untagged)' = OSM rail with no operator tag; 'OHM:(untagged)' = OHM railway ways with no name. No straight-line leg from the router. Starts at the main line near Stillman (drawn MP 8.2 from Munising) with a 216 m straight tie to the routed line. Entirely on OpenHistoricalMap's Munising Railway ways. Waypoints Coalwood, Juniper, Doty, Myren on the line (0.0-0.1 km); Cusino 1.1 km (the hamlet geocode, the end is the nearest point of the OHM grade). Crosses the DSS&A near Juniper/Doty without following it (0.1 mi). Chapman could not be geocoded and was not used. The Munising - Stillman leg is drawn by the Munising - Lawson feature.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] [OPEN both ends] East Branch Stillman - Coalwood - Roscoe - Juniper - Doty (Manistique & Lake Superior junction) - Hartho - Chapman - Petrel - Masters - Myren - Leroux - Cusino. 1929 exact: '[OG30] EAST BRANCH. October 6, 1929': train 52 Munising 8:30 AM - Stillman 9:45 - Coalwood 9:56 - Juniper 10:15 - Doty 10:50 (connection with the M&LS) - Chapman 11:15 - Petrel - Myren 11:40 - Cusino; train 53 back 1:20 PM, arr. Munising 4:50 PM, daily except Sunday. This is ONE proven year: service certainly ran wider both ways but no other year is confirmed. The line began as Munising Railway logging track (Stillman - Acker 1898, MRR-MUN) and was later extended east; when passenger trains started is unknown. A Feb 1951 Guide heading 'EAST BRANCH. February, 1951.' survives in the OCR WITHOUT times, so 1951 is neither confirmed nor denied. Wikipedia's (uncited) 1931 'one [train] on the east branch from Munising to Shingleton' is not supported by the 1929 table. Logging extension Cusino - Sunrise Landing 1957-1965 was freight - not drawn. Do not widen without evidence. headway_min = one train a day (1929).
